items.title: No need to hack when it’s leaking: Artex edition
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Zack Whittaker reports: Security researchers have discovered hundreds of copies of a Chinese-made AI hacking tool publicly exposed to the internet for anyone to access, potentially allowing outsiders to launch cyberattacks against unsuspecting targets. The hacking software, called Artex, is an open source autonomous penetration testing tool, meaning software that automatically probes computer systems for...</article>

items.title: County of Sussex, New Jersey Notice of Data Privacy Incident
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>November 6, 2026 8:00 PM EST NEWTON, N.J., Nov. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — Sussex County Prosecutor’s Office (SCPO) experienced a data privacy event that involved personal information. On or about August 10, 2026, SCPO received alerts of a disruption to its computer network. Upon this identification, it launched an immediate investigation and engaged outside cybersecurity...</article>

items.title: Coding Agents Copy Your Secrets to a Hidden File. Thousands Are on GitHub
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Shmulik Cohen and Matan Giladi write: Apiiro research found 2,539 real secrets in 1,994 public GitHub repositories: database passwords, cloud keys, API tokens, SSH root logins. Among them: a database vendor’s own admin-level cloud key, a production Azure Postgres password, a Square production token, and the owner password of a medical-records database. 63 organizations, mostly...</article>

items.title: Norad targeted by cyberattack
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>From Norway’s aid agency, Norad, November 3: Norad has been targeted by a cyberattack in which the perpetrators may have gained access to the names and email addresses of 20,614 registered users of Norad’s Grant Portal. In addition, they extracted information related to grant applications submitted by at least three organizations. Norad is still working...</article>

items.title: State attorneys general secure up to $10 million and corrective action plan from Perry Johnson companies after 2023 breach
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>A press release from NYS Attorney General Letitia James: NEW YORK – New York Attorney General Letitia James and a coalition of three other attorneys general today secured $10 million from Perry Johnson & Associates, Inc. (PJ&A), Perry Johnson, Inc. (PJI), Perry Johnson & Associates Coding, Inc., Perry Johnson & Associates Radiology, Inc., and Medical...</article>

items.title: The Next Target for Data Breach Lawsuits – Law Firms That Represent Breached Parties
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Mark Rasch writes: Imagine a company gets hacked and hires a law firm to manage the response. The lawyers coordinate the forensic investigation, determine which notification laws apply, and advise management about what to disclose and when. Months later, the notices arrive. The affected individuals sue the company and add its lawyers as defendants. Their...</article>

items.title: NI: Parents warned to be on alert after school data breach
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Robbie Meredith reports: Parents have been told to be alert for unexpected emails or phone calls after a Northern Ireland school app used by almost 50,000 people was affected by a data breach. The Equipple app is used by many schools to schedule and book meetings between parents and teachers. There have been concerns that...</article>

items.title: DigiCert data breach exposes customer information, identity documents
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Lawrence Abrams reports: DigiCert warns it suffered a data breach after a server migration mistakenly exposed an internal business system to the internet, allowing unauthorized access to customer information and identity documents. The certificate authority says the breach affected a small portion of its archived customer data, including names, business email addresses, phone numbers, and...</article>

items.title: Any long password will do: SSH flaw lets hackers into Alpine systems, routers and more
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Ernestas Naprys reports: A massive decade-old flaw affects Alpine and other distributions that run OpenSSH on the musl library. Containers, routers, IoT devices, and other applications are critically vulnerable. Emergency updates are available. Any long password, between 257 and 1024 characters, unlocks thousands of Linux systems via SSH (Secure Shell), the industry standard for remote...</article>

items.title: Ninth Circuit: Breach Of Confidence Confers Standing In Health Data Security Case
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Claire E. Castles, Amanda Fitzsimmons, Nathaniel P. Garrett, Rebekah Byers Kcehowski, Mary Alexander Myers, and Alexander H. Southwell of Jones Day write: Departing from the risk-based approach many courts have applied since TransUnion, and in tension with other circuits, the Ninth Circuit held that health plan participants whose confidential health information was disclosed without authorization...</article>

items.title: UK: Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust data breach exposed health details of 7,715 staff
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Lee Trewhela reports: The Royal Cornwall Hospitals Trust (RCHT) has admitted a huge data breach has led to many affected staff experiencing “significant distress, loss of trust and ongoing anxiety”. The breach exposed sensitive personal health information relating to almost 8,000 current and former staff. An Excel spreadsheet published in February 2023 exposed hidden sickness...</article>

items.title: Anthropic won’t fix a Claude Dispatch flaw that could let attackers execute remote commands across corporate boundaries
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Jessica Lyons reports: A vulnerability in Anthropic’s Claude products lets any browser extension that can control Claude Dispatch make Claude Desktop run code on the computer – or even a different machine signed into the same Claude account – with no browser exploit and minimal user interaction required. Anthropic, aware of the problem since May,...</article>

items.title: Korean court keeps Coupang’s record data breach fine in force, delays corrective action plan for 30 days
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>There’s yet another update in the Coupang data breach case. Previous coverage on DataBreaches.net of the incident, enforcement actions, and Coupang’s objections to the fines and enforcement actions can be found in links under this update. Now Jeong Hye-Jeong reports: A Seoul court on Thursday rejected Coupang’s request to suspend a 423.6 billion won ($315.6 million) fine...</article>

items.title: Canadian man extradited to the U.S. for his role in computer hacking scheme targeting universities
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>November 3, 2026: ROCHESTER, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that a federal grand jury has returned an indictment charging Ryan James Roach, 35 of Saskatchewan, Canada, and Mathiew James Stubbings, 41, of Ontario, Canada, with conspiracy to obtain information from a protected computer and to cause damage to a protected computer, obtaining information from a...</article>

items.title: Lab 1 warns breach data now exposes thousands more firms
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Mara Sugue reports: Lab 1 has published a report analysing 328 million files from 2,089 datasets exposed after cyber attacks. It found that the median breach now exposes data linked to 542 organisations beyond the named victim. The study also found that 13,436 unique organisations were exposed through incidents recorded between 2025 and 2026, underlining...</article>

items.title: Student Data Breach Affects Up to 16 Icelandic Schools
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Iceland Review reports: A security breach affected Inna, the student-information system used by Icelandic upper-secondary schools. It allowed a student to attempt to alter other pupils’ grades and attendance records. Iceland’s Data Protection Authority has received three notifications, while schools and the system operator are still investigating what information may have been accessed. Schools discovered...</article>

items.title: Hackers steal 320,000 UK school files and publish them on dark web
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Nicole Wootton-Cane reports: At least 320,000 school files stolen during a cyber attack on Bristol City Council’s servers have been found posted to the dark web. Hackers targeted the council’s Trading with Schools platform and accessed data from 39 schools across the region in September. The council said specialist investigations have now identified a “significant...</article>

items.title: Cyberattack wipes cloud data at major Russian hosting provider Beget
items.author: Dissent
items.content: <article>Daryna Antoniuk reports: A major Russian web hosting provider is struggling to restore its services after a cyberattack destroyed data across its cloud infrastructure and disrupted hundreds of websites. Beget, one of Russia’s largest domain registrars and hosting companies, said Wednesday that it had begun bringing some servers back online following the attack, which took...</article>
